nodes.name: Pt electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: Pt was electrodeposited from a 1 mM H₂PtCl₆ (99.995%, Aldrich) solution onto fluorine-doped tin-oxide coated glass (Hartford Glass). A square wave pulsed deposition was used, referenced to a Ag quasi-reference electrode (AgQRE). The three-step deposition sequence consisted of a 0.5 s pulse at -0.9 V versus AgQRE, followed by a 0.5 s pulse at -0.2 V versus AgQRE, followed by a 1 s rest interval. The sequence was repeated 120 times, totalling 4 min.
nodes.source_text: Pt was electrodeposited from a 1 mM H₂PtCl₆ (99.995%, Aldrich) solution onto an inert substrate—fluorine-doped tin-oxide coated onto glass (Hartford Glass)... The sequence was repeated 120 times, totalling 4 min.

nodes.name: Pt film annealing
nodes.procedure: The electrodeposited Pt film was heated in a furnace at 500°C in air for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: After heating the initial polycrystalline Pt film in a furnace (see the Methods section)... All heat treatments were conducted in a tube furnace at 500°C in air for 12 h.

nodes.name: Bi underpotential deposition
nodes.procedure: A submonolayer of Bi_ir was adsorbed onto the annealed Pt film by Bi UPD: 10 min immersion in 1 mM Bi₂O₃/0.5 M H₂SO₄ solution, resulting in ~10% Bi_ir coverage by XPS.
nodes.source_text: We then adsorbed a submonolayer of Bi_ir onto the Pt film by the same Bi UPD method used in previous reports (10 min, 1 mM Bi₂O₃/0.5 M H₂SO₄), resulting in an estimated Bi_ir coverage of ~10% by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy

nodes.name: BiPt alloy formation annealing
nodes.procedure: The Pt-Bi_ir precursor was annealed in a tube furnace at 500°C in air for 12 h to form the BiPt surface alloy. This heating step provides the temperature necessary for Bi to overcome kinetic barriers and alloy into the Pt surface layer.
nodes.source_text: To complete the synthesis of a BiPt surface alloy, we annealed the Pt-Bi_ir precursor to 500°C in a tube furnace... All heat treatments were conducted in a tube furnace at 500°C in air for 12 h.

nodes.description: HER performance of initial annealed Pt film

normalization.value: surface area of initial pure Pt sample

nodes.source_text: After heating the initial polycrystalline Pt film in a furnace (see the Methods section), the sample demonstrated a current density of i_{0.0 V} = 5.6(10)^{-4} A cm_{pt}^{-2} (-log i_{0.0 V} = 3.25 ), consistent with previous literature values for Pt and indicating that the starting material was prepared adequately with negligible contamination.

nodes.description: HER performance immediately after Bi UPD on Pt film

electrolyte.value: 1 mM Bi2O3 / 0.5 M H2SO4 (for Bi UPD)

HER_activity.value: considerably less than initial Pt film

nodes.source_text: We then adsorbed a submonolayer of Bi_ir onto the Pt film by the same Bi UPD method used in previous reports (10 min, 1 mM Bi2O3 / 0.5 M H2SO4 ), resulting in an estimated Bi_ir coverage of ~10% by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy... Immediately after Bi UPD, the measured activity of the Pt-Bi_ir sample was considerably less than that of the initial Pt film—as expected, the Bi_ir blocked Pt sites and poisoned the surface for hydrogen evolution.

nodes.description: HER performance of BiPt surface alloy after second annealing at 500°C

normalization.value: surface area of initial pure Pt sample

nodes.source_text: Having completed the annealing procedure, we again measured the hydrogen evolution rate. Figure 5 shows significantly improved current–voltage characteristics; quantitatively speaking, i_{0.0 V} is double that of the Pt-Bi_ir precursor and, more importantly, ~50% greater than i_{0.0 V} of the initial Pt film.

nodes.description: Control experiment: HER performance of pure Pt after multiple heat treatments
nodes.source_text: To verify that the final anneal did not influence the Pt itself, we conducted several control experiments on similarly prepared pure Pt samples through multiple heat treatments. These data are shown as an inset in Fig. 5 and demonstrate a negligible effect.
